summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Lewis Addison Grant (1828–1918), who worked as a teacher and lawyer before serving as a Union Army soldier in the American Civil War. He later became United States Assistant Secretary of War. The note says he was among the leading officers from Vermont and received the Medal of Honor for personal gallantry and intrepidity.
one_line: Biography of Lewis Addison Grant, Vermont-born teacher, lawyer, Union Army officer, Medal of Honor recipient, and later U.S. Assistant Secretary of War.
key_facts: Lewis Addison Grant was born on January 17, 1828.
Lewis Addison Grant died on March 20, 1918.
Lewis A. Grant was a teacher and lawyer before his military service.
Lewis A. Grant was a soldier in the Union Army during the American Civil War.
Lewis A. Grant later served as United States Assistant Secretary of War.
Lewis A. Grant was among the leading officers from the state of Vermont.
Lewis A. Grant received the Medal of Honor.
The Medal of Honor citation for Lewis A. Grant describes his "personal gallantry and intrepidity."
